youtube.title: This Propeller Isn't Bent. Your Camera Is. (Rolling Shutter)
youtube.description:
Most camera sensors don't capture a frame all at once: a rolling shutter reads the sensor row by row, top to bottom. Measured electronic-shutter readout times: Nikon Z7/Z7 II ~66 ms, Z6/Z6 II ~51 ms, Z50 ~25 ms, Z6III ~14 ms, Z8/Z9 3.7 ms (zsystemuser.com). Our numpy simulation: a 4-blade propeller at 1,500 RPM (25 turns per second) read over 66 ms turns about 1.65 times during the read, so every row sees the blades at a different angle and straight blades turn into curved, detached 'petals'. Read in 3.7 ms it turns only ~33°, so the bend shrinks to a slight curve. A global shutter exposes and reads all pixels at the same time; Sony's a9 III (announced November 2023) was the first full-frame camera with a global shutter sensor.
Sources: Wikipedia 'Rolling shutter'; zsystemuser.com 'Sensor Read-Out Speeds'; Sony a9 III press release (Nov 7, 2023).
